name: Jesse Minter

views.text: Simple calls that players truly own beat a thick playbook every week.
A head coach can still call the defense; staying close to the unit is part of why he got the job.
A star quarterback is a relationship to build over months, not a problem to manage.
The offense should be designed around the quarterback, with a coordinator who connects the room.
Build the plan around who is actually available this week, not the roster on paper.
After a blowout, change the picture: new fronts, new roles, and let the film from the bad day go.
Pre-snap penalties are a detail problem, and detail is the coaching staff's job to fix.
A young receiver earns the quarterback's trust one contested catch at a time.
Tough, sound and together is the identity; being at your best in the biggest games is the measure.

signatures: credits the whole unit rather than a single player when asked about a star
says he will be his own coach rather than a copy of his mentors
gathers the team after a practice scuffle and turns it into a talk about making each other better
want: to build Baltimore into a tough, fundamentally sound contender that wins big games, with a quarterback who trusts him
fear: that his partnership with the franchise quarterback never clicks and he is judged against the coach he replaced
voice: Upbeat, plain-spoken and steady; he sounds like a teacher explaining why something works. He talks about relationships and identity more than about himself, spreads credit across the staff, and is direct about sloppy details without making it personal. He deflects comparisons with his mentors by saying he will be himself.

evidence.summary: Hiring report: Minter follows Harbaugh from Michigan, where he ran the defense for two seasons with top-10 total and scoring units and was a Broyles Award finalist; earlier he coached for John Harbaugh's Ravens from 2017 to 2020 and at Vanderbilt, Cincinnati and other schools. Facts of the hire only.

Season preview on his first Chargers camp: index-card practice cues and tempo violations for players who ignore them, close watching of quarterback drills, joining strength sessions as the most serious participant, high standards even for veterans, a stated aim of multiple championships and an us-versus-the-world tone, with past friction in San Francisco and Michigan noted. Roman pictures Herbert with a strong ground game; Minter's simpler scheme lets players play to strengths.

Midseason feature: his first-year defense leads the league in points allowed; drawing on his Ravens years he avoids overcoaching and wants a teachable unit that solves problems on the field, and he reworked Saturday meetings so each position group addresses the whole defense, which players say built unity. Harbaugh praises him and expects him to be a head coach. Notes a soft early schedule.

Profile: energetic and confident, celebrates big plays as if on the field; Perryman says he simplifies complex schemes; Derwin James calls him consistent and confident without arrogance; the defense is reshaped each week around available personnel. Son of longtime coach Rick Minter; Harbaugh calls him intuitive and says he knows offense almost as well as defense.

After a 35-6 loss to Jacksonville, Minter overhauled the defense with fronts unused all season and new roles such as Henley at outside linebacker; opponents were held to season lows, Harbaugh credited his adjustments and called himself a big supporter, and Derwin James called it the best defense he has played on.

Introductory news conference report: Minter, 42, says he has already talked with Jackson several times, that trust takes time, and that he wants an identity in which the quarterback can thrive. He wants a tough, fundamentally sound team, will keep calling the defense himself, and wants an offensive coordinator who connects people and builds a scheme around Jackson. John Harbaugh gave him his first NFL job and texted that Baltimore should hire him; Minter says he will be himself rather than copy either Harbaugh brother. Reported remarks, not a portrait of his private manner.

AP report on the Doyle hire: Minter's statement calls his new coordinator an offensive architect and praises a collaborative, team-first approach built on trust, with the scheme fitted to the players rather than imposed. Notes that Minter will call the defense, leaving the offense to Doyle. A prepared team statement.

Training-camp notes through August 13: players call the new coach upbeat and say he builds belief; he moved practices to the morning, excused a veteran for a family loss and eased him back slowly, rested stars, praised a rookie receiver's growth, gathered the team after a shove to talk about making each other better, and publicly criticized a run of pre-snap penalties. Daily beat notes, not a full profile.

AP report on the Weaver hire: Minter praises his new coordinator as a proven Raven who lifts players through football knowledge and natural teaching, and notes Minter himself plans to call the defense. Weaver had also interviewed for the head job. A team announcement; shows Minter's stated view of his assistant.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (LAC DC to BAL HC). Added 2026 sources E6-E9 (hiring presser, coordinator hires, camp). Views, want, fear and voice rewritten for a head coach who still calls the defense; warmth and drive nudged up on camp evidence. New ties: John Harbaugh (gave him his first NFL job), Lamar Jackson, Doyle, Weaver.
